1.title: AI Cannot Reliably Run a Company for Six Months | Richard Ngo
1.author: MTS
1.hook: Richard Ngo (ex-OpenAI governance, DeepMike safety) argues recursive self-improvement timelines are overhyped, explains why AI capabilities remain jagged, and diagnoses alignment field as bottlenecked by conceptual confusion and political groupthink rather than raw capability gaps.

1.title: 10 Habits PhDs Must Unlearn To Build a Startup | Startup School
1.author: Y Combinator
1.hook: YC partner and PhD-turned-founder Francois Chaubard breaks down 10 mindset shifts from academic research to startup building — covering the difference between interesting vs. important ideas, working without external structure, first-mover disadvantages, and why delegation of hard problems fails.

2.title: Wharton’s Top AI Professor: Stop Starting Software Companies — The Real AI Money Is Here
2.author: Silicon Valley Girl
2.hook: Ethan Mollick (Wharton AI Labs) on managing AI agents without cognitive surrender — when to hand off vs. keep doing yourself, why experts get more from AI than juniors, workflow for agent use, and the risk of over-trusting agent output.

3.title: Why AI Research Won't Hit Fast Takeoff | Charlie O'Neill
3.author: MTS
3.hook: Charlie O'Neill (Baseten) argues recursive self-improvement and fast takeoff timelines are overstated due to compute constraints and RL bottlenecks; discusses why automating ML research hits diminishing returns; covers Baseten's new inference and agent platform.

4.title: Why the Cultural Monoculture Is Officially Over | Ruby Thelot
4.author: MTS
4.hook: Analysis of cultural fragmentation using 11 years of Wikipedia traffic data, Billboard streaming patterns, and niche market growth (adult toys) to argue monoculture has fractured into algorithmic curation and platform-driven subcultures.
